text.p: Rowan Cos said Monday if business conditions continued to improve at the current rate, its earnings for 1997 could be in the range of $160 million or $1.80 a share.
At the same time, the company said it intends to call for redemption on April 1 $50 million of its $200 million outstanding 11-7/8 percent senior notes due December 1, 2001.
It said the notes will be redeemed at 106 percent of the principal amount plus accrued interest from December 1, 1996 to the redemption date.
C. R. Palmer, chairman and chief executive officer said the continued improvement in the offshore driling business gave the company confidence to begin an accelerated debt reduction program.

He said the company's average dayrate for the first quarter of 1997 should exceed $45,000, while 15 of its 21 offshore rigs are now committed to driling programs into the third quarter at rates averaging more than $50,000 a day.
Because of the improving conditions, Palmer said that beyond 1997, "Who knows -- we may someday pay a dividend to our investors."

Rowan, which provides domestic and international contract drilling and aviation services, previously reported net income per share of $0.27 for the fourth quarter of 1996, up from $0.07 for the comparable quarter in 1995.
